headline: SK Hynix Scraps Solidigm US IPO After Shareholder Concerns
author: Yoolim Lee

paragraphs.text: Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:52 PM MST 1 min read

(Bloomberg) -- SK Hynix Inc. has scrapped plans for a US listing of its Solidigm unit after facing strong shareholder opposition and regulatory scrutiny over concerns that the move could undermine minority investor interests.
The South Korean chipmaker has also halted a pre-IPO investment process that was being pursued alongside the listing, according to a regulatory filing on Friday.
Solidigm, SK Hynix's flash-memory subsidiary, had selected Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley as lead banks for a potential US listing next year.

The reversal follows concerns by South Korean regulators that the planned offering could amount to a "duplicate listing," potentially diluting the interests of existing shareholders. Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin told lawmakers earlier this week that both the Financial Services Commission and his agency viewed Solidigm as falling under restrictions on duplicate listings.

The controversy had become a test of Seoul's efforts to strengthen corporate governance and minority shareholder protections as it seeks to address the country's chronic equity undervaluation, known as the "Korea discount."
